name: Anji's Binary Tree
statement: Anji has a binary tree with n vertices rooted at 1. Each vertex has a letter 'U', 'L', or 'R'. If you are at vertex u with letter 'L', you move to left child; 'R' to right child; 'U' you don't move. You can modify any vertex's letter to any of 'U', 'L', 'R'. Find the minimum number of modifications so that you can reach some leaf starting from the root.
key_insight: Tree dynamic programming where dp[u] is minimum modifications to reach a leaf in u's subtree: dp[u] = min(dp[left] + [s[u]!='L'], dp[right] + [s[u]!='R']).

name: Count the Number of Pairs
statement: You are given a string s of lowercase and uppercase Latin letters and an integer k. You can perform at most k operations: convert a lowercase letter to uppercase or vice versa. A pair is formed by one uppercase and one lowercase instance of the same letter. Find the maximum number of pairs you can form.
key_insight: Greedily match existing lowercase and uppercase pairs, then convert leftover duplicate letters of the same case using at most k operations.

name: We Were Both Children
statement: There are n frogs at coordinate 0. The i-th frog hops by ai units per second. A trap is placed at some integer coordinate x from 1 to n. A frog is caught if its hop sequence lands on x. Find the maximum number of frogs that can be caught by placing a single trap at an optimal coordinate x <= n.
key_insight: Harmonic series iteration: count frequency of each step size a <= n, then for each a add count to all its multiples j <= n in O(n log n) total time.

name: Polygon
statement: A polygon has an n x n square grid. Cannons on the top and left borders shoot '1's into the matrix. A '1' travels down or right until it hits another '1' or the matrix border. Given the final matrix of '0's and '1's, determine if this configuration could have been created by a sequence of valid cannon shots.
key_insight: For any '1' not on the bottom row or rightmost column, it must be supported by a '1' directly below it or directly to its right.

name: The Lakes
statement: You are given an n x m grid of non-negative integers representing water depths. A lake is a maximal connected component of cells with depth > 0 connected 4-directionally. The volume of a lake is the sum of depths of all cells in it. Find the maximum volume of a lake.
key_insight: Standard connected component search using DFS/BFS to sum cell depths in each 4-directional positive component.

name: K-th Not Divisible by n
statement: You are given two positive integers n and k. Print the k-th positive integer that is not divisible by n.
key_insight: Each block of n numbers contains exactly (n-1) non-divisible numbers. The k-th number is k + floor((k-1)/(n-1)).

name: Building an Aquarium
statement: You have n columns of heights a1, a2, ..., an. You want to build a tank of height h such that pouring water to level h requires at most x units of water. Water needed is sum(max(0, h - ai)). Find the maximum integer height h.
key_insight: Water required is monotonically non-decreasing with height h, so binary search on h over the range [1, 2e9].

name: Ski Resort
statement: A skier can ski on days where temperature is at most q. The skier wants to ski for at least k consecutive days. Given temperatures of n days, find the total number of valid continuous vacation intervals of length >= k where every day has temperature <= q.
key_insight: Decompose into maximal contiguous segments of valid days with length L >= k; each segment contributes (L - k + 1)*(L - k + 2)/2 subsegments.

name: Yarik and Array
statement: An array is good if adjacent elements have alternating parities. Find the maximum sum of a non-empty subarray that is good.
key_insight: Kadane's algorithm modified: reset the running sum whenever two adjacent elements have the same parity or when running sum drops below 0.

name: Plus Minus Permutation
statement: Given n, x, y, construct a permutation of 1..n to maximize the score: sum of elements at indices divisible by x minus sum of elements at indices divisible by y.
key_insight: Common multiples of x and y cancel out. Assign the largest available numbers from n downwards to indices uniquely divisible by x, and smallest numbers 1 upwards to indices uniquely divisible by y.

name: Ice Cream Balls
statement: You want to create exactly n distinct pairs of ice cream balls. Two balls with different flavors count as 1 distinct type of 2-ball ice cream. Two balls with the same flavor count as 1 distinct type. What is the minimum total number of balls needed?
key_insight: Using k distinct flavors gives C(k, 2) pairs. The remaining n - C(k, 2) pairs can be achieved by adding 1 duplicate ball for each required extra pair.

name: Assembly via Minimums
statement: An array a of n integers was used to form an array b of n*(n-1)/2 elements where b contains min(a_i, a_j) for all 1 <= i < j <= n. You are given array b in random order. Reconstruct any possible original array a.
key_insight: When sorted, the smallest element of a appears n-1 times in b, the second smallest appears n-2 times, etc. Sample values by advancing indices by n-1, n-2, ..., 1.

name: Rudolph and Christmas Tree
statement: Rudolph has a Christmas tree with n identical isosceles triangle branches, each with base d and height h. The i-th branch's base is at height y_i. Find the total area covered by the tree branches without double counting overlapping regions.
key_insight: Overlapping portion of consecutive triangles forms a smaller similar triangle of height overlap_h = y_i + h - y_{i+1}; subtract its area.

name: Vlad Building Beautiful Array
statement: An array is beautiful if all elements are positive and have the same parity. You can replace ai with ai - aj for any j != i. Determine if you can make all elements in array a have the same parity and remain strictly positive.
key_insight: All-even is possible only if there are no odd numbers. All-odd is possible if and only if the global minimum is odd (so evals can subtract min_odd and become positive odd).

name: Gold Rush
statement: You have a pile of n gold coins. If the pile size is divisible by 3, you can split it into two piles of sizes 2n/3 and n/3. Can you ever obtain a pile of exactly m coins by repeating this process?
key_insight: Direct recursive branch check: at each state n, branch to n/3 and 2n/3 with pruning when n < m or n is not divisible by 3.

name: Odd Queries
statement: Given an array a of n integers, answer q queries: if elements from index l to r are replaced with value k, will the sum of all elements in the array become odd?
key_insight: Use 1D prefix sum array to answer each range replacement query in O(1) time.

name: Negatives and Positives
statement: Given an array a of n integers. You can multiply any two adjacent elements by -1 any number of times. Find the maximum possible sum of the array.
key_insight: Flipping signs of adjacent elements preserves parity of negative counts. If total negatives is even, all elements can be made positive; if odd, leave the element with minimum absolute value negative.

name: Binary Inversions
statement: You are given a binary array a of length n. You can flip at most one element (0 to 1 or 1 to 0). An inversion is a pair (i, j) with i < j and a_i = 1, a_j = 0. Find the maximum number of inversions after at most one flip.
key_insight: Optimal flip is either flipping the first 0 to 1 or the last 1 to 0 (or making no flips).

name: Scuza
statement: There is a staircase of n steps with step heights a1, a2, ..., an. Timur has legs of length k. He can climb steps as long as the step height <= k. For q queries with leg length k, find the maximum height (sum of step heights climbed) Timur can reach.
key_insight: Maintain prefix maximums of step heights. For each query k, use binary search (`std::upper_bound`) to find the farthest reachable step and return its prefix sum.

name: Binary Deque
statement: You have a deque of n binary elements (0s and 1s). In one operation, you can remove one element from the front or the back. Find the minimum number of operations to make the sum of remaining elements in the deque equal to s, or -1 if impossible.
key_insight: Minimizing removed elements from ends is equivalent to maximizing the length of a contiguous subarray with sum equal to s using sliding window / two pointers.
